bookInfo.name: Old History of the Five Dynasties

title.zh: 卷十二 梁書12: 宗室列傳二
title.en: Volume 12 Book of Later Liang 12: Biographies 2 - Imperial Family
title.raw: 卷十二 梁書12: 宗室列傳二 Volume 12 Book of Later Liang 12: Biographies 2 - Imperial Family

sentences.zh: 廣王全昱，太祖長兄，受禪後封。

translations.literal: Prince of Guang Quan Yu was the Founder's eldest brother; enfeoffed after receiving the abdication.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Yu, Prince of Guang, was the Founder's eldest brother and received his princely title when the dynasty was founded.

sentences.zh: 乾化元年，還睢陽，命內臣拜餞都外。

translations.literal: In Qianhua year 1, he returned to Suiyang; the Emperor ordered inner-court attendants to perform farewell rites outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianhua he went back to Suiyang; court eunuchs were sent outside the city to bid him farewell.

sentences.zh: 王出宿至於偃師，仍詔其子衡王友諒侍從以歸。

translations.literal: The Prince departed, lodged overnight reaching Yanshi; moreover an edict ordered his son Prince of Heng You Liang to attend and accompany him home.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he spent a night at Yanshi; an edict also directed his son You Liang, Prince of Heng, to escort him home.

sentences.zh: 庶人篡位，授宋州節度使。

translations.literal: When the commoner usurped the throne, [he] was appointed military commissioner of Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the usurper Zhu Youzhen seized power, Quan Yu was made military commissioner of Song.

sentences.zh: 貞明二年，卒。

translations.literal: In Zhenming year 2, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Zhenming.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《五代會要》：全昱，贈尚書令，諡德靖。

translations.literal: (《Five Dynasties Essentials》: Quan Yu was posthumously given Minister of Works; posthumous title Dejing.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》 records that Quan Yu was posthumously honored as Minister of Works with the temple name Dejing.

sentences.zh: 《五代史闕文》：全昱，梁祖之兄也。

translations.literal: 《Lacunae of the History of the Five Dynasties》: Quan Yu was elder brother of the Liang Founder.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Lacunae of the History of the Five Dynasties》 identifies Quan Yu as the Liang founder's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 既受禪，宮中開宴，惟親王得與。

translations.literal: After receiving the abdication, the palace held banquets; only imperial princes were permitted to attend.
translations.idiomatic: Once the dynasty was founded, palace feasts were held to which only imperial princes were admitted.

sentences.zh: 因為博戲，全昱酒酣，忽起取骰子擊盆迸散，大呼梁祖曰：「朱三，汝碭山一民，因天下饑荒，入黃巢作賊，天子用汝為四鎮節度使，富貴足矣，何故滅他李家三百年社稷，稱王稱朕，吾不忍見血吾族矣，安用博為！

translations.literal: During gambling, Quan Yu, wine deep, suddenly rose, took dice and struck the bowl scattering them, loudly calling to the Liang Founder: "Zhu Third! You, a commoner of Dangshan—because the realm suffered famine you entered Huang Chao's bandits as a thief; the Son of Heaven used you as military commissioner of four circuits—wealth and honor are enough—why destroy the Li family's three hundred years of state altars, call yourself king and emperor? I cannot bear to see our clan's blood shed—what need for gambling!"
translations.idiomatic: At dice play Quan Yu, drunk, leaped up, smashed the bowl with his dice, and shouted at the Liang founder: "Zhu Third! You were a peasant from Dangshan who joined Huang Chao's rebels in famine; the throne made you lord of four circuits—that should have been enough. Why wipe out the Li dynasty's three-century altars and call yourself king and Son of Heaven? I will not watch our family slaughtered—why gamble at all!"

sentences.zh: 」梁祖不悅而罷。

translations.literal: " The Liang Founder was displeased and broke up [the party].
translations.idiomatic: The founder took offense and ended the feast.

sentences.zh: 臣護按《梁史》《廣王全昱傳》曰：昱樸野，常呼帝為「三」。

translations.literal: Your subject Hu annotates: 《History of Liang》《Biography of Prince of Guang Quan Yu》 says: Yu was rustic and uncouth, often calling the Emperor "Third."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhu notes in the 《History of Liang》 biography of Prince Guang that Quan Yu was coarse and habitually addressed the emperor as "Third."

sentences.zh: 宮中博戲之事諱之。

translations.literal: Palace gambling affairs were tabooed.
translations.idiomatic: Gambling in the palace became a forbidden topic.

sentences.zh: 夫梁祖弑二君，弑一皇后，名臣被害者不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Now the Liang Founder murdered two sovereigns, murdered one empress; famous ministers murdered—countless beyond recording.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang founder had killed two emperors and an empress, and slaughtered famous ministers beyond count.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗即位，盡誅朱氏，惟全昱先令終。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he executed the entire Zhu clan; only Quan Yu had earlier died a natural death.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong came to power he killed the whole Zhu house; only Quan Yu had already died in his bed.

sentences.zh: 至道初，知單州有稱廣王之後與尼訟田者，豈以一言之善，獨存其嗣耶！）〉

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhidao, it was known at Shan prefecture there was one claiming to be descendant of Prince of Guang disputing fields with a nun—could it be that for one good saying alone his posterity was preserved?!)〉
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhidao reign a man at Shan prefecture claiming descent from Prince Guang sued a nun over land—did a single honest speech alone spare his line?!)〉

sentences.zh: 友諒，全昱子，初封衡王，後嗣廣王。

translations.literal: You Liang, son of Quan Yu, first enfeoffed Prince of Heng, later inherited Prince of Guang.
translations.idiomatic: You Liang, Quan Yu's son, was first Prince of Heng and later succeeded to the title Prince of Guang.

sentences.zh: 繼曆藩郡，多行不法。

translations.literal: Successively holding various prefectural domains, he often acted unlawfully.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in succession across the provinces he repeatedly broke the law.

sentences.zh: 坐弟友能反，廢囚京師。

translations.literal: Implicated because younger brother You Neng rebelled, deposed and imprisoned in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When his brother You Neng rose in revolt he was stripped of rank and imprisoned at court.

sentences.zh: 唐師入汴，與友能、友誨同日遇害。

translations.literal: Tang troops entered Bian; with You Neng and You Hui he was killed on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang armies took Bian he was executed the same day as You Neng and You Hui.

sentences.zh: 友誨，全昱子，封邵王。

translations.literal: You Hui, son of Quan Yu, enfeoffed Prince of Shao.
translations.idiomatic: You Hui, another son of Quan Yu, held the title Prince of Shao.

sentences.zh: 乾化元年，以檢校兵部尚書充控鶴指揮使。

translations.literal: Qianhua year 1, with acting Minister of War served as commander of the Crane-Control Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianhua 1 he served as acting Minister of War and commander of the Crane-Control Guard.

sentences.zh: 坐友能反廢，後為唐兵所殺。

translations.literal: Implicated in You Neng's rebellion and deposed; later killed by Tang troops.
translations.idiomatic: Disgraced for You Neng's revolt, he was later slain by Tang forces.

sentences.zh: 安王友寧，字安仁，少習詩禮，長喜兵法，有倜儻之風。

translations.literal: Prince of An You Ning, style Anren, in youth studied Poetry and Rites, in maturity delighted in military methods, had a bold and unbounded air.
translations.idiomatic: You Ning, Prince of An (courtesy name Anren), studied the classics as a boy and warfare as a man, with a dashing temper.

sentences.zh: 太祖鎮汴，累署軍職，每因出師，多命統驍果以從。

translations.literal: When the Founder governed Bian, repeatedly appointed to army posts; whenever campaigns arose he was often ordered to lead fierce warriors in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Founder's rule at Bian he rose through army commands and usually led elite troops on campaign.

sentences.zh: 及擒秦宗權，太祖令友寧監送宗權西獻於長安，詔加檢校右散騎常侍、行右監門衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Qin Zongquan was captured, the Founder ordered You Ning to supervise escorting Zongquan west to present at Chang'an; edict added acting Right Palace Attendant and Acting Right Supervisor of the Palace Gate Guards.
translations.idiomatic: After the capture of Qin Zongquan the Founder sent You Ning to escort him to Chang'an; the court promoted him to acting palace attendant and acting gate guard commander.

sentences.zh: 自是繼立軍功，累官至檢校司空兼龔、柳二州刺史。

translations.literal: From then on he repeatedly achieved military merit, rising through offices to acting Minister of Works concurrently prefect of Gong and Liu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he won repeated victories and rose to acting Minister of Works while governing Gong and Liu.

sentences.zh: 太祖駐軍岐下，遣友寧領所部兵先歸梁苑，以備守禦。

translations.literal: The Founder encamped below Qi, dispatched You Ning to lead his troops first back to Liang Garden to prepare defense.
translations.idiomatic: While the Founder camped near Qi he sent You Ning ahead with his division to secure the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 屬青帥王師範構亂，以關東諸鎮兵悉在岐、隴，欲乘虛竊發，自齊、魯至於華下，羅布奸黨，皆詐以委輸貢奉為名，陰與淮夷、並門結好。

translations.literal: At this time the Qing military commissioner Wang Shifan plotted rebellion; because all eastern-pass troops were at Qi and Long, he wished to strike while the realm was empty—from Qi and Lu down to below Hua he spread secret agents, all falsely under the name of delivering tribute, while secretly allying with Huaiyi and Bingmen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shifan of Qingzhou rebelled, hoping to exploit the absence of eastern armies at Qi and Long: from Shandong to the Guanzhong frontier he planted agents posing as tribute missions while secretly courting Huainan and Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 會有青人詣裴迪言其狀，迪以事告，友寧不俟命乃率兵萬餘人東討。

translations.literal: It happened a man of Qing came to Pei Di and reported the situation; Di told the affair, and You Ning without awaiting orders led more than ten thousand troops east to punish.
translations.idiomatic: A Qing informer told Pei Di, who reported to You Ning; without waiting for orders You Ning marched east with ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 師範遣其弟將兵圍齊州。

translations.literal: Shifan sent his younger brother to lead troops and besiege Qi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan sent his brother to lay siege to Qi prefecture.

sentences.zh: 友寧引兵救之，青寇大敗，奪馬四千蹄，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: You Ning led troops to rescue; Qing bandits were greatly defeated, seizing four thousand horse hooves, beheading several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: You Ning relieved the city and routed the Qing forces, taking four thousand horses and thousands of heads.

sentences.zh: 及昭宗歸長安，朝廷議迎駕功，友寧授嶺南西道節度使，加特進、檢校司徒，賜號迎鑾毅勇功臣。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong returned to Chang'an, the court discussed merit in welcoming the imperial carriage; You Ning was given military commissioner of Lingnan West Circuit, advanced to Special Grandee and acting Minister of Works, granted the title Meritous Minister Who Welcomes the Imperial Carriage with Resolute Courage.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhaozong's return to Chang'an the court rewarded those who had escorted him: You Ning became military commissioner of Lingnan West, Special Grandee, and acting Minister of Works, with the honorific Welcoming-the-Carriage Resolute Warrior.

sentences.zh: 時青寇數千，越險潛伏，欲入兗州。

translations.literal: At the time several thousand Qing bandits, crossing rugged terrain, lay hidden, wishing to enter Yan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand Qing raiders were moving through the hills toward Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 友寧知之，伏兵於兗南邀之，大破賊眾，竟無免者。

translations.literal: You Ning knew it, ambushed troops south of Yan to intercept them, greatly defeating the bandit host; in the end none escaped.
translations.idiomatic: You Ning set an ambush south of Yan, destroyed the force, and left no survivor.

sentences.zh: 自是兗壁危窘，友寧督諸軍進逼營兵。

translations.literal: From then on the Yan ramparts were perilous and strained; You Ning supervised the armies pressing the rebel camp.
translations.idiomatic: With Yanzhou hard pressed, You Ning drove his columns against the rebel encampment.

sentences.zh: 首攻博昌縣，月餘未能拔。

translations.literal: First attacking Bochang county, more than a month unable to take it.
translations.idiomatic: He first assaulted Bochang but failed to capture it for over a month.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒，遣劉捍督戰。

translations.literal: The Founder was angry and dispatched Liu Han to supervise the battle.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder, enraged, sent Liu Han to take command of the siege.

sentences.zh: 友寧乃下俘民眾十餘萬，各領負木石、牽牛驢，於城南為土山。

translations.literal: You Ning then released more than a hundred thousand captive common people, each leading and bearing timber and stone, driving oxen and donkeys, building an earthen mound south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: You Ning drove more than a hundred thousand captives—each hauling timber and stone behind oxen and donkeys—to heap an assault ramp south of the walls.

sentences.zh: 既至，合人畜木石排而築之，冤枉之聲，聞數十里。

translations.literal: When complete, men and beasts, timber and stone were ranged and piled; cries of injustice were heard for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: As the ramp rose, human and animal labor was driven in ranks; wails of the dying carried for miles.

sentences.zh: 俄而城陷，盡屠其邑人，清河為之不流。

translations.literal: Shortly the city fell; the entire populace of the district was slaughtered, and the Qing River ceased to flow.
translations.idiomatic: The city soon fell and every inhabitant was massacred until the Qing River ran thick with blood.

sentences.zh: 及進迫寇壘，與青人戰於石樓，王師小卻，友寧旁自峻阜馳騎以赴敵，所乘馬蹶而仆，遂沒於陣。

translations.literal: When advancing to press the rebel fortress, fighting Qing troops at Shilou, Wang's army slightly retreated; You Ning from a steep height galloped to meet the enemy, his mount stumbled and fell, and he perished in the formation.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the rebel stronghold at Shilou, he charged from a ridge when Wang's line wavered; his horse fell and he died in the melee.

sentences.zh: 友寧將戰之前日，有大白蛇蟠於帳中，友寧心惡之，既而果遇禍焉。

translations.literal: The day before You Ning was to fight, a great white serpent coiled in his tent; You Ning's heart hated it, and afterward he indeed met calamity.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of battle a great white snake coiled in his tent—an omen he loathed—and the next day he was killed.

sentences.zh: 密王友倫，幼聰悟，喜筆劄，曉聲律。

translations.literal: Prince of Mi You Lun, in youth clever and perceptive, delighted in letters, understood musical tones.
translations.idiomatic: You Lun, Prince of Mi, was bright as a child, loved literature, and had an ear for music.

sentences.zh: 及長，好騎射，有經度之智，太祖每奇之，曰：「吾家千里駒也。

translations.literal: When grown, he loved riding and shooting, had the wisdom of governance; the Founder often marveled at him, saying: "A thousand-li colt of our house.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he excelled at horsemanship and archery and showed sound judgment; the Founder often praised him: "He is the fleet steed of our clan.

sentences.zh: 」年十九，為宣武軍校。

translations.literal: " At nineteen he became an officer of the Xuanwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: " He entered the Xuanwu Army as an officer at nineteen.

sentences.zh: 景福初，充元從騎軍都將，尋表為右武衛將軍，漸委戎事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingfu, he served as commander of the personal cavalry guard; soon memorialized as Right Martial Guard general, gradually entrusted with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingfu he commanded the emperor's mounted guard, was soon made Right Martial Guard general, and gradually took on field command.

sentences.zh: 太祖征兗、鄆，友倫勒所部兵收聚糧穀，以濟軍須。

translations.literal: When the Founder campaigned against Yan and Yun, You Lun led his troops to gather grain to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: During campaigns in Yan and Yun he gathered grain for the army.

sentences.zh: 幽、滄軍至內黃，友倫前鋒夜渡河擊賊，奪馬千匹，擒斬甚眾。

translations.literal: You and Cang troops reached Neihuang; You Lun's vanguard crossed the river by night to strike bandits, seizing a thousand horses, capturing and beheading many.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhou and Cangzhou forces reached Neihuang, his vanguard crossed the river at night, took a thousand horses, and killed or captured many.

sentences.zh: 因引兵往八議關，卒逢晉軍萬餘騎，友倫乃分布兵士，多設疑軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led troops toward Bayi Pass, suddenly encountering more than ten thousand Jin cavalry; You Lun then distributed soldiers, setting many decoy units.
translations.idiomatic: Marching toward Bayi Pass he met more than ten thousand Jin horsemen and spread his men in feigned formations.

sentences.zh: 因聲鼓誓眾，士伍奮躍，追斬數十里。

translations.literal: Thereupon beating drums and swearing the host, the ranks leaped forward, pursuing and beheading for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: He drummed the troops to an oath, they charged, and the pursuit ran for miles.

sentences.zh: 其後，李罕之請以上黨來歸，為晉軍所圍。

translations.literal: Afterward Li Hanzhi requested to submit Shangdang and return to allegiance, but was besieged by Jin troops.
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Hanzhi offered to surrender Shangdang but was besieged by Jin forces.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣友倫總步騎數萬，越險救應，遂大破晉軍。

translations.literal: The Founder dispatched You Lun to command several tens of thousands of foot and horse, crossing rugged terrain to rescue and respond, and greatly defeated Jin troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder sent You Lun with tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry over difficult ground to relieve him and routed the Jin army.

sentences.zh: 唐朝加檢校司空、守藤州刺史。

translations.literal: The Tang court added acting Minister of Works, acting prefect of Teng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tang promoted him to acting Minister of Works and acting prefect of Teng.

sentences.zh: 天復元年，岐、隴用兵，晉人乘虛侵於北鄙。

translations.literal: In Tianfu year 1, troops were used at Qi and Long; Jin men took advantage of emptiness to invade the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 1, while war raged at Qi and Long, Jin raiders struck the northern border.

sentences.zh: 友倫率徒兵三萬徑往礬山，晉人望塵奔逸。

translations.literal: You Lun led three thousand foot soldiers straight to Fanshan; Jin men fled at sight of dust.
translations.idiomatic: You Lun marched three thousand foot soldiers to Fanshan and the Jin army fled at his approach.

sentences.zh: 友倫與氏叔琮等躡其轍，追至太原，摩壘挑戰，獲牛馬萬餘。

translations.literal: You Lun with Shi Shuzong and others followed their tracks, pursuing to Taiyuan, pressing the ramparts and challenging battle, obtaining more than ten thousand cattle and horses.
translations.idiomatic: With Shi Shuzong he pursued to Taiyuan, challenged the walls, and seized more than ten thousand cattle and horses.

sentences.zh: 二年，領所部兵西赴鳳翔，前後累接戰。

translations.literal: Year 2, he led his troops west to rush to Fengxiang, before and after repeatedly joining battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he marched west to Fengxiang and fought a series of engagements.

sentences.zh: 三年，昭宗歸長安，製授友倫寧遠軍節度使、檢校司徒，賜號迎鑾毅勇功臣。

translations.literal: Year 3, Zhaozong returned to Chang'an; by decree You Lun was made military commissioner of the Ningyuan Army, acting Minister of Works, granted the title Meritous Minister Who Welcomes the Imperial Carriage with Resolute Courage.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, after Zhaozong's return, You Lun became Ningyuan military commissioner and acting Minister of Works with the honorific Welcoming-the-Carriage Resolute Warrior.

sentences.zh: 及太祖東歸，留友倫宿衛京師。

translations.literal: When the Founder returned east, he left You Lun to garrison and guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder went east he left You Lun to guard Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，因會賓擊鞠，墜馬而卒。

translations.literal: After more than a year, while meeting guests playing cuju, he fell from a horse and died.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he fell from his horse during a polo match with guests and died.

sentences.zh: 昭宗輟視朝一日，詔贈太傅，歸葬於碭山縣。

translations.literal: Zhaozong suspended court audience for one day, edict posthumously gave Grand Tutor, burial returned to Dangshan county.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong mourned him with a day without court and posthumously made him Grand Tutor; he was buried in Dangshan.

sentences.zh: 開平初，有司上言曰：「東漢受命，伯升預其始謀；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiping, the relevant office memorialized saying: "When Eastern Han received the Mandate, Bo Sheng took part in the initial planning;
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiping the authorities reported: "When the Eastern Han received Heaven's mandate, Bo Sheng shared in the founding design;

sentences.zh: 西周尚親，叔虞荷其封邑。

translations.literal: Western Zhou honored kin; Shu Yu bore its enfeoffed domain.
translations.idiomatic: the Western Zhou cherished kin, and Shu Yu received his fief.

sentences.zh: 故皇兄存，凋零霜露，綿曆歲時，恩莫逮於陟岡，禮方宏於事日。

translations.literal: Therefore the imperial elder brother Cun, withered by frost and dew, spanning years in time—kindness could not reach the mound on the hill, rites should be enlarged for the day of service.
translations.idiomatic: Our elder imperial brother Cun lies long in the grave; years have passed without fitting rites at his tomb.

sentences.zh: 皇侄故邕州節度使友寧、故容州節度使友倫，頃因締構，俱習韜鈐，並以戰功，歿於王事，永言帶礪，合議封崇。

translations.literal: Imperial nephew, late Yongzhou military commissioner You Ning, late Rongzhou military commissioner You Lun—recently because of founding the structure, both studied military manuals, and both through battle merit died in royal service; forever speaking of belt and flint, together we should discuss enfeoffment and elevation.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial nephews You Ning, late commissioner of Yong, and You Lun, late commissioner of Rong, were trained in war from the founding days and died in service; they deserve posthumous honors befitting founders of the house.

sentences.zh: 」於是存追封朗王，友寧追封安王，友倫追封密王。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Cun was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Lang, You Ning posthumously Prince of An, You Lun posthumously Prince of Mi.
translations.idiomatic: " Cun was posthumously created Prince of Lang, You Ning Prince of An, and You Lun Prince of Mi.

sentences.zh: 郴王友裕，字端夫，太祖長子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Chen You Yu, style Duanfu, was the Founder's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: You Yu, Prince of Chen (courtesy name Duanfu), was the Founder's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 幼善射禦，從太祖征伐，性寬厚，頗得士心。

translations.literal: In youth skilled at shooting and driving; followed the Founder in campaigns; nature generous and thick, considerably won soldiers' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Trained in archery and horsemanship, he campaigned with the Founder, won troops by his easy manner.

sentences.zh: 唐中和中，太祖會並帥李克用攻圍華州，賊將黃鄴固守甚堅。

translations.literal: In the Zhonghe era of Tang, the Founder joined Bing military commissioner Li Keyong to besiege Hua prefecture; bandit general Huang Ye held firm defense extremely solid.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang Zhonghe the Founder and Li Keyong besieged Hua prefecture, where the rebel Huang Ye held the walls stubbornly.

sentences.zh: 俄有一人登陴大詈，克用令北騎連射，終不能中，命友裕射之，應弦而斃。

translations.literal: Shortly a man ascended the wall and cursed loudly; Keyong ordered northern cavalry to shoot in succession, ultimately unable to hit; he ordered You Yu to shoot, and at the bowstring's release [the man] died.
translations.idiomatic: A man on the wall shouted abuse; Keyong's northern archers could not bring him down, but You Yu's arrow killed him on the first shot.

sentences.zh: 大軍喜噪，聲震山谷，克用因以良弓百矢遺焉。

translations.literal: The great army rejoiced and clamored, sound shaking mountains and valleys; Keyong therefore with a hundred good bows and arrows gifted him.
translations.idiomatic: The army roared until the hills echoed; Keyong rewarded him with a hundred fine bows.

sentences.zh: 太祖鎮汴，表為宣武軍牙校。

translations.literal: When the Founder governed Bian, memorialized as Xuanwu Army junior officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder held Bian he was made a junior officer of the Xuanwu Army.

sentences.zh: 及蔡賊殄滅，朝廷議功，加檢校左僕射，尋為牙內馬步都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Cai bandits were exterminated, the court discussed merit, added acting Left Vice Minister of Works, soon made commander of all inner palace horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: After the destruction of the Cai rebels the court rewarded him with acting Left Vice Minister of Works and soon commander of the inner horse-and-foot guard.

sentences.zh: 景福元年，總大軍伐徐。

translations.literal: Jingfu year 1, commanded the great army to attack Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingfu 1 he led the main force against Xu.

sentences.zh: 時朱瑾領兗、鄆之眾，為徐戎外援，陣於彭門南石佛山下。

translations.literal: At the time Zhu Jin led Yan and Yun hosts as outer support for Xu bandits, arrayed below Stone Buddha Mountain south of Peng Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jin of Yan and Yun brought allied troops to aid Xu and drew up south of Pengmen at Stone Buddha Mountain.

sentences.zh: 友裕縱兵擊之，斬獲甚眾，瑾領殘黨宵遁。

translations.literal: You Yu loosed troops to strike them, beheading and capturing very many; Jin led the remnant party to flee by night.
translations.idiomatic: You Yu attacked, inflicted heavy losses, and Jin fled by night with the survivors.

sentences.zh: 時都虞候朱友恭羽書聞於太祖，誣友裕按兵不追賊，太祖大怒，因驛騎傳符，令裨將龐師古代友裕為帥，仍令按劾其事。

translations.literal: At the time Chief Commandant Zhu You Gong's urgent dispatch reached the Founder, falsely accusing You Yu of holding troops and not pursuing bandits; the Founder was greatly angry, and through post-horse transmitted tally, ordered deputy general Pang Shigu to replace You Yu as commander, still ordering investigation of the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Commandant Zhu You Gong reported that You Yu had held his men back; the Founder, furious, sent Pang Shigu by relay to replace him and investigate.

sentences.zh: 會使人誤致書於友裕，友裕懼，遂以數騎遁於山中。

translations.literal: It happened the messenger mistakenly delivered the letter to You Yu; You Yu was afraid, and with several horsemen fled into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: A courier misdelivered the order to You Yu, who fled into the hills with a few riders.

sentences.zh: 尋詣廣王於輝州，以訴其冤。

translations.literal: Shortly he went to Prince of Guang at Hui prefecture to plead his injustice.
translations.idiomatic: He soon sought out Prince Guang at Hui prefecture to plead his case.

sentences.zh: 賴元貞皇后聞而召之，令束身歸汴，力為營救，太祖乃舍之，令權知許州。

translations.literal: Relying on Empress Yuanzhen hearing and summoning him, ordered him to bind himself and return to Bian, vigorously pleading rescue; the Founder then released him, ordered temporary charge of Xu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yuanzhen intervened, had him return to Bian in custody, and secured his pardon; the Founder then put him in temporary charge of Xu.

sentences.zh: 乾寧二年，加檢校司空，尋為武寧軍節度留後。

translations.literal: Qianning year 2, added acting Minister of Works, soon made acting military commissioner of the Wuning Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianning 2 he was made acting Minister of Works and soon acting Wuning military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四年，太祖下東平，改天平軍留後，加檢校司徒。

translations.literal: Year 4, the Founder descended on Dongping, changed to acting Tianping Army commissioner, added acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, after the Founder took Dongping, he became acting Tianping commissioner with acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 光啟元年，再領許州。

translations.literal: Guangqi year 1, again held Xu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangqi 1 he again governed Xu.

sentences.zh: 天復初，為奉國軍節度留後。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu, made acting military commissioner of the Fengguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianfu he became acting Fengguo military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 太祖兼鎮河中，以友裕為護國軍節度留後，尋遷華州節度使，加檢校太保、興德尹。

translations.literal: When the Founder concurrently governed Hezhong, made You Yu acting Huguo Army military commissioner, soon moved to Hua military commissioner, added acting Grand Guardian and Xingde Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder also held Hezhong he made You Yu acting Huguo commissioner, then Hua commissioner, Grand Guardian, and Xingde intendant.

sentences.zh: 天祐元年七月，兼行營都統，領步騎數萬，經略邠、岐。

translations.literal: Tianyou year 1, seventh month, concurrently acting commander of all campaign armies, leading several tens of thousands of foot and horse, administering Bin and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Tianyou 1 he became campaign commander-in-chief with tens of thousands of troops operating in Bin and Qi.

sentences.zh: 十月，友裕有疾，將校乃謀旋師，尋卒於梨園，歸葬東京。

translations.literal: Tenth month, You Yu had illness; officers then plotted to withdraw the army; shortly he died at Liyuan, burial returned to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he fell ill; his officers prepared to withdraw, and he died at Liyuan and was buried in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 開平初，追贈郴王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiping, posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiping he was posthumously created Prince of Chen.

sentences.zh: 乾化三年，又贈太師。

translations.literal: Qianhua year 3, again posthumously given Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianhua 3 he was further posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 博王友文，本姓康，名勤，太祖養以為子，受禪後封為王。

translations.literal: Prince of Bo You Wen, original surname Kang, name Qin; the Founder adopted him as son, after receiving the abdication enfeoffed as prince.
translations.idiomatic: You Wen, Prince of Bo, born Kang Qin, was adopted by the Founder and enfeoffed after the founding of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 為東京留守，嗜酒，頗怠於為政。

translations.literal: Served as regent of the Eastern Capital, addicted to wine, considerably slack in governing.
translations.idiomatic: As Eastern Capital regent he drank heavily and neglected government.

sentences.zh: 友珪弑逆，並殺友文。

translations.literal: You Gui murdered and usurped; together killed You Wen.
translations.idiomatic: When You Gui murdered the Founder he killed You Wen as well.

sentences.zh: 末帝即位，盡復官爵。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, fully restored office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor restored his titles in full.

sentences.zh: 友珪，小字遙喜，母失其姓，本亳州營妓也。

translations.literal: You Gui, childhood name Yaoxi; mother lost her surname—originally a camp courtesan of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: You Gui, childhood name Yaoxi, was born to a Bozhou camp courtesan whose family name is unknown.

sentences.zh: 唐光啟中，帝徇地亳州，召而侍寢。

translations.literal: In the Guangqi era of Tang, the Emperor toured Bozhou territory, summoned her to attend his bed.
translations.idiomatic: During Tang Guangqi, while campaigning in Bozhou, the Founder took her to his bed.

sentences.zh: 月餘，將舍之而去，以娠告。

translations.literal: After more than a month, about to leave her and depart, she reported pregnancy.
translations.idiomatic: After a month he was about to leave when she told him she was with child.

sentences.zh: 是時，元貞皇后賢而有寵，帝素憚之，由是不果攜歸大梁，因留亳州，以別宅貯之。

translations.literal: At the time Empress Yuanzhen was worthy and held favor; the Emperor always feared her, and therefore did not succeed in bringing [the mother] back to Great Liang, but left her at Bozhou, storing her in a separate residence.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder feared his capable consort Yuanzhen and never brought the woman to the capital, keeping her in a separate house at Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 及期，妓以生男來告，帝喜，故字之曰遙喜。

translations.literal: When the term came, the courtesan reported bearing a male child; the Emperor rejoiced, therefore styled him Yaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: When she bore a son he was delighted and gave the boy the childhood name Yaoxi.

sentences.zh: 後迎歸汴。

translations.literal: Later welcomed back to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Mother and son were later brought to Bian.

sentences.zh: 受禪後封郢王。

translations.literal: After receiving the abdication, enfeoffed Prince of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: After the founding of the dynasty he was created Prince of Ying.

sentences.zh: 開平四年十月，檢校司徒，充左右控鶴都指揮使，兼管四蕃將軍。

translations.literal: Kaiping year 4, tenth month, acting Minister of Works, served as commander of the Left and Right Crane-Control Guards, concurrently supervising the Four Barbarian Generals.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Kaiping 4 he became acting Minister of Works, commander of the Left and Right Crane-Control Guards, and overseer of the Four Barbarian Generals.

sentences.zh: 乾化元年，充諸軍都虞候。

translations.literal: Qianhua year 1, served as chief commandant of all armies.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianhua 1 he was made chief commandant of all armies.

sentences.zh: 二年，弑太祖篡位，均王以兵討之，自殺，追廢為庶人。

translations.literal: Year 2, murdered the Founder and usurped the throne; Prince of Jun led troops to punish him; he killed himself, posthumously deposed as commoner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he murdered the Founder and seized the throne; Prince of Jun marched against him; he committed suicide and was posthumously degraded to commoner.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《五代會要》云：郢王友珪，開平元年五月九日封，至乾化二年六月三日篡位，偽改鳳曆元年。

translations.literal: (《Five Dynasties Essentials》 says: Prince of Ying You Gui, on the ninth day of the fifth month of Kaiping year 1 enfeoffed, until the third day of the sixth month of Qianhua year 2 usurped the throne, falsely changed to Fengli year 1.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》 records that You Gui, Prince of Ying, was enfeoffed on the ninth day of the fifth month of Kaiping 1, usurped on the third day of the sixth month of Qianhua 2, and proclaimed the false era Fengli.

sentences.zh: 三月十七日，京城軍亂，侍衛袁象先率兵入宮，友珪自殺。

translations.literal: Third month, seventeenth day, capital army mutiny; Palace Guard Yuan Xiangxian led troops into the palace; You Gui killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth day of the third month the capital garrison mutinied; Palace Guard Yuan Xiangxian stormed the palace and You Gui took his own life.

sentences.zh: 少帝即位，追削為庶人。

translations.literal: When the Lesser Emperor took the throne, posthumously stripped to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The Lesser Emperor posthumously reduced him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 又載：周廣順中，張昭修實錄，奏云：梁末帝之上，有郢王友珪，篡弑居位，未有紀錄，請依《宋書》劉劭例，書為「元凶友珪」。

translations.literal: Also recorded: In the Guangshun era of Zhou, Zhang Zhao revised the Veritable Records, memorializing: Above the Last Emperor of Liang was Prince of Ying You Gui, who usurped and murdered and held the throne, with no record yet—request according to 《Song History》 Liu Shao's precedent to write as "Arch-rebel You Gui."
translations.idiomatic: The same source adds: In Later Zhou Guangshun, Zhang Zhao revised the Veritable Records and proposed that You Gui, who had murdered his way to the throne above the Last Emperor, be entered—as with Liu Shao in the 《History of Song》—under the title "Arch-rebel You Gui."

sentences.zh: 案《梁實錄》今無考。）〉

translations.literal: Case: 《Liang Veritable Records》 now has no examination.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The 《Liang Veritable Records》 cited here are no longer extant.)〉

sentences.zh: 福王友璋，太祖第五子，受禪後封。

translations.literal: Prince of Fu You Zhang, the Founder's fifth son, enfeoffed after receiving the abdication.
translations.idiomatic: You Zhang, Prince of Fu, was the Founder's fifth son and received his title at the founding.

sentences.zh: 賀王友雍，太祖第六子，受禪後封。

translations.literal: Prince of He You Yong, the Founder's sixth son, enfeoffed after receiving the abdication.
translations.idiomatic: You Yong, Prince of He, was the Founder's sixth son and was enfeoffed when the dynasty was founded.

sentences.zh: 建王友徽，太祖第七子，受禪後封。

translations.literal: Prince of Jian You Hui, the Founder's seventh son, enfeoffed after receiving the abdication.
translations.idiomatic: You Hui, Prince of Jian, was the Founder's seventh son and received his title at the founding.

sentences.zh: 康王友孜，太祖第八子，末帝即位後封，以反誅。

translations.literal: Prince of Kang You Zi, the Founder's eighth son, enfeoffed after the Last Emperor took the throne, executed for rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: You Zi, Prince of Kang, the Founder's eighth son, was enfeoffed under the Last Emperor and executed for treason.
